questions.stem: Will copper react with zinc sulfate solution?

options.text: Yes, because copper is more reactive than zinc
Yes, because all metals react with sulfate solutions
No, because copper is less reactive than zinc and cannot displace it
No, because zinc sulfate is insoluble

questions.explanation: Copper will not react with zinc sulfate solution because copper is below zinc in the reactivity series. A less reactive metal cannot displace a more reactive metal from its compound, so no reaction occurs.

questions.stem: In the displacement reaction between iron and copper sulfate, which half-equation correctly shows what happens to the copper ions?
questions.explanation: In this displacement reaction, the copper ions (Cu²⁺) gain two electrons to form copper metal: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. This is reduction (gain of electrons). The iron is oxidised (Fe → Fe²⁺ + 2e⁻), providing the electrons that the copper ions gain.
